editorial: When an 11‑year‑old finds his programming‑broken robot has no set of instructions, you’re immediately pulled into a world where a glitch feels like a glitch of your own life. Its coming‑of‑age script reimagines the toy‑friend trope by making the machine’s imperfections a mirror for childhood anxieties, a concept that feels both fresh and relatable. A lively hand‑drawn neon palette, combined with clever audio cues, turns every malfunction into a visual gag that keeps the pace lively. There’s a brief mid‑film slowdown as the plot searches for its footing, but the final act rescues the momentum with an emotional payoff. If you love family adventures that flirt with satire and want a narrative that puts humor and heart on equal footing, you’ll find this animated, sci‑fi comedy worth the watch.
targetAudience: Ideal for fans of family adventures that blend humor with heartfelt moments.
